---
title: "Want to Contribute?"
format: html
---

I believe teaching is, at its core, about collaboration. The best classroom activities are rarely invented in isolation. They're passed between colleagues, tweaked in a tutorial, refined after a lecture that didn't quite land, and shared over a coffee break. Some of the hooks on this site started life exactly that way, borrowed and adapted from other educators generous enough to share what worked (and what did not) for them.

That's the spirit behind making this resource open access. Good teaching materials shouldn't sit locked away in one person's slide deck, only ever used once a year by one class. The hope is that by putting these hooks out in the open, other educators can pick them up, adapt them to their own courses, and hopefully build on them further, the same way I've built on ideas from others.

If you have an activity, demonstration, or story you think would work well here, I'd love to hear about it. Chances are you've got a hook of your own that consistently gets a room's attention, and this collection only gets better the more perspectives it draws on.

Feel free to reach out at [minh.huynh1@monash.edu](mailto:minh.huynh1@monash.edu). You'll of course be credited for your contribution — or, if you'd rather stay behind the scenes, you're welcome to remain anonymous.
